summary: Accepted PR #4537 extends the existing skill-quality entry with --preflight BASE_SHA and runs the same cheap path before its normal engine build. Reuse the real Atlas delivery checks and the full fixture's partial skill-tree link predicate: archive-only validation missed omitted bundled seeds, and repository-present test links failed in the partial tree. Local integration review exposed a further join: importing Atlas generated ignored __pycache__ bytes in one skill mirror, causing the canonical manifest check to fail after a superficially successful preflight. The maintained route suppresses Python bytecode throughout and rejects existing caches or changes to delivered skill bytes before any engine build. Real controls retain both original hosted defect classes and the local bytecode failure, including normal-entry blocking and zero CLR/engine sentinel launches; clean preflight followed by canonical projection/manifest validation was independently accepted. The corrected local complete command was observed at about two seconds, with OS cache state uncontrolled and active repair effort uninstrumented. Full semantic, compiler and required hosted qualification remains intact; a final body-only status edit also incurred metadata-sensitive requalification, retained separately from source work. Neither cheap scope nor source/hosted success establishes process containment, native execution authority, two-workload capacity, installed receiver adoption or comparative savings. Preserve V3-IMPROVE-01.1's open second-workload/cohort assertions and its inconclusive economics; this is a correctness improvement, not a wider-rollout or speedup claim.
title: Preflight the assembled carrier and preserve delivered skill bytes
